````markdown
![[Meeting notes#^budget]]

### A table marked on the line below

![[Meeting notes#^costs]]
````

PDF:

![Embedded note, heading, block and table](../img/features/embed-notes.png)

| Syntax | Embeds |
| ------ | ------ |
| `![[Note]]` | The whole note. |
| `![[Note#Heading]]` | The heading and its content, up to the next heading of the same or a higher level. |
| `![[Note#A#B]]` | Heading `B` inside section `A`. |
| `![[Note#^id]]` | The block marked `^id`, see [Block IDs](block-ids.md). |
| `![[Note#^id-id]]` | A range, see [Block Link Plus](../plugins/block-link-plus.md). |

Embedded content is processed like the note it comes from:

- Plugin syntax (Dataview, Meta Bind, ...) uses the frontmatter and folder of the source note.
- Images and wiki links resolve from the source note's folder.
- Embeds inside embedded content are expanded too, up to 10 levels. An embed that would include itself again is skipped.
- Headings are shifted so the topmost one sits one level below the heading the embed is under. Without a heading above it, the page title counts. Nested headings keep their relative levels.
- An embed alone on its line (it may be indented, or in a quote or callout) becomes block content. An embed alone in a list item (`- ![[Note#^id]]`) becomes block content of that item, so an embedded callout, list or table keeps its form. An embed inside other text is inserted inline, with its lines joined.
- A note, heading or block that cannot be found shows as italic text, such as _Note#^id_, and the export prints a warning.

The target is looked up in the whole vault. `![[Note]]` picks the closest note of that name. A path such as `![[Folder/Note#^id]]` is matched against the end of each note's path.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/block-ids/

# Block IDs

A block ID (`^id`) at the end of a line marks that paragraph, list item or heading. A line with only `^id` marks the block right above it: a table, list, quote or callout. The IDs are used by [embeds](embeds.md#notes-headings-and-blocks) and removed from the output.

Markdown:

````markdown
Block IDs at the end of a line are removed from the output. ^first-point

- A list item with an ID ^item

> A quote with an ID on the line below

^quote
````

PDF:

![Text with the block IDs removed](../img/features/block-ids.png)

`^id-id` marks the end of a range for [Block Link Plus](../plugins/block-link-plus.md). Without that plugin it is a plain block ID.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/callouts/

# Callouts

## Types

Every Obsidian callout type works. Aliases share the style of their group: `[!summary]` looks like `[!abstract]`, `[!caution]` like `[!warning]`.

Markdown:

````markdown
> [!note]
> note

> [!abstract]
> abstract, summary, tldr

> [!info]
> info

> [!todo]
> todo

> [!tip]
> tip, hint, important

> [!success]
> success, check, done

> [!question]
> question, help, faq

> [!warning]
> warning, caution, attention

> [!failure]
> failure, fail, missing

> [!danger]
> danger, error

> [!bug]
> bug

> [!example]
> example

> [!quote]
> quote, cite
````

PDF:

![Every callout type with its colour](../img/features/callout-types.png)

| Group | Types |
| ----- | ----- |
| note | `note` |
| abstract | `abstract`, `summary`, `tldr` |
| info | `info` |
| todo | `todo` |
| tip | `tip`, `hint`, `important` |
| success | `success`, `check`, `done` |
| question | `question`, `help`, `faq` |
| warning | `warning`, `caution`, `attention` |
| failure | `failure`, `fail`, `missing` |
| danger | `danger`, `error` |
| bug | `bug` |
| example | `example` |
| quote | `quote`, `cite` |

Any other type, such as `[!information]`, looks like a note unless the template styles it.

## Titles, folding, nesting

Markdown:

````markdown
> [!tip] A custom title
> The title replaces the type name.

> [!faq]- Foldable callouts are always shown open
> The `+` and `-` markers are accepted.

> [!warning] Nested callouts
> Outer text.
>
> > [!info] Inner callout
> > Inner text.

> [!note] Lazy continuation
A line without `>` still belongs to the callout,
as in Obsidian.

| Status | Note |
| ------ | ---- |
| Done   | > [!success] Inline callout in a cell |
````

PDF:

![Custom title, foldable, nested, lazy and inline callouts](../img/features/callouts.png)

- The text after the type is the title. Without it, the type name is the title.
- The fold markers `[!faq]+` and `[!faq]-` are accepted. The callout is always shown open.
- Callouts nest with `> >`.
- Blank `>` lines stay inside the callout.
- A line right after a callout without `>` still belongs to it (lazy continuation), as in Obsidian.
- A callout can start a list item (`- > [!note]`) or be indented under one. It stays a callout box inside that item.
- A single-line callout inside other text, for example in a table cell, becomes an inline callout.

## HTML and CSS

A callout becomes a `div` with the classes of its type and group, and a `data-callout` attribute:

```html
  <p><span class="callout-title"><strong>Title</strong></span></p>
  <p>Text</p>
```

An inline callout is a `span` with the same classes. To style a type, see the [CSS reference](../templating/css-reference.md#callouts).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/highlights-comments/

# Highlights and comments

## Highlights

`==text==` becomes `<mark>`.

Markdown:

````markdown
Mark the ==important words== in a sentence.

==A whole line can be highlighted.==
````

PDF:

![Highlighted words and a highlighted line](../img/features/highlights.png)

## Comments

`%% ... %%` comments, on one line or over several lines, and HTML comments are removed. Inside code they stay as written.

Markdown:

````markdown
This text is visible. %% This comment is not. %%

%%
A comment block over several lines
is removed as well.
%%

<!-- HTML comments are removed too. -->
The `%% text %%` inside code stays as written.
````

PDF:

![Only the visible text remains](../img/features/comments.png)

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/tags/

# Tags

Inline tags such as `#draft` or `#area/docs` stay in the text as plain text. Tags in the frontmatter are not shown. The [Dataview](../plugins/dataview.md) plugin uses both kinds for `FROM #tag` queries.

Markdown:

````markdown
Tags such as #draft and #status/review stay in the text as written.

Nested tags like #area/docs/pdf are kept as well.
````

PDF:

![Tags as plain text](../img/features/tags.png)

A tag at the start of a line is not a heading, because headings need a space after `#`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/properties/

# Properties

The properties block (YAML frontmatter) at the top of a note is parsed and removed from the output. [Meta Bind](../plugins/meta-bind.md) and [Dataview](../plugins/dataview.md) read it.

Markdown:

````markdown
---
title: Release checklist
owner: Docs team
tags: [release, checklist]
---
The properties block at the top is parsed and removed. Plugins such as Meta Bind and Dataview read it.

The owner of this page is `VIEW[{owner}][text]`.
````

PDF:

![The frontmatter is gone, a Meta Bind view shows one value](../img/features/properties.png)

The title of the document comes from `--title` or the folder name, not from a `title` property.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/tasks/

# Tasks

`- [ ]` and `- [x]` become empty and checked boxes on the same line as the text, in a list without bullets.

Markdown:

````markdown
- [ ] Write the release notes
- [x] Update the version
- [ ] Review the PDF
    - [x] Check the table of contents
    - [ ] Check the footer
````

PDF:

![Open and done tasks, nested](../img/features/tasks.png)

The list is a `ul.task-list`. Status characters other than space and `x` (such as `[/]` or `[-]` from some themes) are not drawn as boxes.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/line-breaks/

# Line breaks

In Obsidian a single newline is a line break, unless "Strict line breaks" is on. ope reads that setting from `.obsidian/app.json` (`strictLineBreaks`).

Markdown:

````markdown
A single newline
is a line break,
as in Obsidian.

A blank line starts a new paragraph.
````

PDF:

![A newline is a line break](../img/features/line-breaks.png)

With strict line breaks, or with `-O line_breaks=soft`, lines of one paragraph are joined:

Markdown:

````markdown
A single newline
is a line break,
as in Obsidian.

A blank line starts a new paragraph.
````

PDF:

![Lines joined into one paragraph](../img/features/line-breaks-soft.png)

| Option | Effect |
| ------ | ------ |
| `-O line_breaks=hard` | A newline is always a line break. |
| `-O line_breaks=soft` | A newline is a space. A line break needs two trailing spaces or a backslash. |

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/mermaid/

# Mermaid

` ```mermaid ` blocks are drawn as SVG by [Pele](https://pele.run), a Mermaid renderer in TypeScript by the Obsidian team. ope runs it in the JavaScript engine that also runs [DataviewJS](../plugins/dataview.md), so it needs no Node.js, npm or browser. It reads Mermaid 12.1 syntax and draws every diagram type Mermaid has, in a few milliseconds per diagram. A block Pele cannot draw, for example because of a syntax error, stays a code block and the export prints a line starting with `Warning:`.

Markdown:

````markdown
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Notes] --> B{Export}
    B -->|PDF| C[Readers]
    B -->|Redline| D[Reviewers]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    Author->>ope: export ./Notes
    ope->>Author: handbook.pdf
```
````

PDF:

![A flowchart and a sequence diagram](../img/features/mermaid.png)

The output is SVG, so text stays sharp and can be searched.

## Options

| Option | Effect | Default |
| ------ | ------ | ------- |
| `-O mermaid=off` | Keep Mermaid blocks as code. | on |
| `-O mermaid.config=PATH` | JSON [Mermaid config](https://mermaid.js.org/config/schema-docs/config.html), such as `themeVariables.fontSize`. | none |
| `-O mermaid.max_height=LENGTH` | Largest height, such as `10cm`. Taller diagrams are scaled down. | none |
| `-O mermaid.landscape=on\|off` | Put wide diagrams on landscape pages. | `on` |
| `-O mermaid.landscape_ratio=R` | Width to height ratio from which a diagram that has to shrink goes to landscape. | `1.4` |
| `-O mermaid.landscape_min_font=PT` | Smallest text size a diagram may shrink to on a portrait page before it goes to landscape, or to fit a tall diagram on one page. | `7` |
| `-O mermaid.fit=on\|off` | Scale or split diagrams that are taller than the page. | `on` |

A template can set a base config with the `mermaid` key in `template.yaml` or `Template.mermaid_config()`. `mermaid.config` is merged over it.

```bash
ope export ./Notes -O mermaid.config=mermaid.json
```

```json
{ "themeVariables": { "fontSize": "14px", "fontFamily": "Georgia, serif" } }
```

Earlier versions drew diagrams with mermaid-cli, which needed Node.js and a headless Chromium. ope no longer uses it. Its options `mermaid.renderer`, `mermaid.theme`, `mermaid.format`, `mermaid.scale`, `mermaid.cli`, `mermaid.puppeteer_config` and `mermaid.trim` have no effect, and the export prints a warning when one is set. `mermaid.renderer=pele` is accepted without a warning.

## Colors and fonts

Pele draws with its own neutral style. Its colors are the CSS variables listed under [Theming](https://pele.run/theming), such as `--pele-fg`, `--pele-surface`, `--pele-border`, `--pele-line`, `--pele-accent` and `--pele-series-1` to `--pele-series-8`. WeasyPrint does not resolve CSS variables in SVG, so ope writes their values into the SVG. They come from the template's CSS:

- The label font is the `font-family` of `body`, the monospace font the one of `code` or `pre`, and the text color the `color` of `body`. Diagrams use the font of the document.
- `themeVariables.fontFamily` in the Mermaid config sets the label font too.
- `themeVariables.fontSize` in the Mermaid config or in the front matter of a diagram sets the base font size.
- `--pele-*` variables in a rule for `:root`, `html`, `body` or `.pele` set any color. They may use `var()` of other custom properties of those rules.

```css
.pele {
  --pele-surface: #eef2f7;
  --pele-border: #6b7f99;
  --pele-accent: var(--color-accent);
}
```

Pele needs the width of every label to lay a diagram out. ope measures them with Pango, the text engine WeasyPrint uses, in the font of the PDF and at the size they are drawn, so labels fit their boxes in any font. When the template font is not installed, labels are measured and drawn in the font that replaces it. Each label is drawn as one line of shaped text, so Arabic letters join, Arabic and Hebrew read from right to left and Hindi or Thai vowel signs stay on their letters.

A character that no installed font has is drawn as `□` (or `?` when no font has `□` either), and the boxes of the diagram are sized for it. The export prints a warning that lists these characters. Install fonts that cover the scripts of the labels, for example Noto, see [Fonts and scripts](../getting-started/installation.md#fonts-and-scripts).

## Differences from Mermaid

Pele reads the same syntax as Mermaid, but it is not mermaid.js. A diagram can look different from the one in Obsidian:

- Pele has its own layout, so boxes and lines can be placed differently.
- Mermaid themes (`theme`, `themeVariables` colors, `themeCSS`) and `%%{init}%%` theme settings are not used. Map colors with `--pele-*` variables in the template instead, see [Colors and fonts](#colors-and-fonts).
- `layout: elk` is not used. Pele always lays a diagram out on its own.
- Links and images in diagrams are turned off.
- `<br>` and `</br>` both break a label into lines.

The Pele build is part of ope (version 1.6.0, MIT license, see the license header of `obsidian_pdf_exporter/core/assets/pele.js`). `scripts/update_pele.py` in the repository replaces it with another version and checks it against the hash the npm registry publishes. CI checks that the stored build is the pinned one.

## Diagram size

A diagram keeps its natural size and only shrinks when it is wider than the text. `mermaid.max_height` scales down taller ones. Other sizes belong in the template's CSS: every diagram has the classes `doc-image`, `mermaid` and `mermaid-<type>`, see [CSS reference](../templating/css-reference.md#mermaid-diagrams).

Pele gives every diagram an exact size with a margin of 8 px, so there is no empty space to trim.

`%%` comment lines in a block are removed before rendering.

## Wide diagrams

A diagram wider than the text shrinks, and so does its text. When that makes it hard to read, the diagram goes to its own landscape page, like a [wide table](../markdown/tables.md#wide-tables).

Markdown:

````markdown
A wide diagram moves to its own landscape page:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Draft] --> B[Review] --> C[Approve] --> D[Export PDF] --> E[Sign] --> F[Publish] --> G[Archive] --> H[Retire]
```

Figure 1: The document life cycle

The text continues on a portrait page.
````

PDF:

![A wide flowchart on a landscape page, with its caption](../img/features/mermaid-landscape.png)

A diagram moves when it has to shrink to fit a portrait page and either its width is at least `mermaid.landscape_ratio` times its height, or its text would get smaller than `mermaid.landscape_min_font` points. It only moves when the landscape page shows it larger, so a tall diagram stays where it is. On the landscape page it is sized to fit the page height, with room for a caption.

A short paragraph right below the diagram that starts with a word and a number, such as `Figure 1: Overview`, is its caption and moves with it. The diagram gets the class `landscape`, its wrapper `wide-table-section landscape-figure`, so a template's landscape page for tables applies to diagrams too.

```bash
ope export ./Notes -O mermaid.landscape_ratio=2
ope export ./Notes -O mermaid.landscape=off
```

## Tall diagrams

A diagram taller than the page would run past the bottom margin. ope keeps every diagram inside the page content box. The size of the page and its margins come from the template, for portrait and landscape pages alike.

- When the diagram's text stays at least `mermaid.landscape_min_font` points tall, the diagram is scaled down to the height of the page. It keeps its aspect ratio. A caption below it stays on the same page.
- Otherwise the diagram is cut into parts that follow each other over several pages. The parts keep the width the diagram had, so the text keeps its size. Each cut goes through a row near the bottom of the page where little is drawn, so it does not go through a box or a line of text when there is a gap between them.

Markdown:

````markdown
A sequence diagram that is taller than the page goes on over two pages:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: Request 1
    S-->>C: Response 1
    C->>S: Request 2
    S-->>C: Response 2
    C->>S: Request 3
    S-->>C: Response 3
    C->>S: Request 4
    S-->>C: Response 4
    C->>S: Request 5
    S-->>C: Response 5
    C->>S: Request 6
    S-->>C: Response 6
    C->>S: Request 7
    S-->>C: Response 7
    C->>S: Request 8
    S-->>C: Response 8
    C->>S: Request 9
    S-->>C: Response 9
    C->>S: Request 10
    S-->>C: Response 10
    C->>S: Request 11
    S-->>C: Response 11
    C->>S: Request 12
    S-->>C: Response 12
    C->>S: Request 13
    S-->>C: Response 13
    C->>S: Request 14
    S-->>C: Response 14
    C->>S: Request 15
    S-->>C: Response 15
    C->>S: Request 16
    S-->>C: Response 16
    C->>S: Request 17
    S-->>C: Response 17
    C->>S: Request 18
    S-->>C: Response 18
```

The text continues after the diagram.
````

PDF:

![A long sequence diagram cut into two parts on two pages](../img/features/mermaid-tall.png)

Every part holds the whole drawing and shows only its band of it, so a search in the PDF also finds the text of the hidden bands. Fitting needs a second layout of the document, which only runs when a diagram is too tall. `-O mermaid.fit=off` turns it off, `mermaid.max_height` gives all diagrams a smaller limit.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/obsidian/bases/

# Bases

[Bases](https://help.obsidian.md/bases) is a core plugin of Obsidian. A base is a `.base` file, or a ` ```base ` code block, in YAML. It selects notes with filters and shows them in views. The export renders a view as it looks when the PDF is made. The notes here are the project notes shown on the [Dataview](../plugins/dataview.md) page.

Markdown:

````markdown
```base
filters:
  and:
    - file.hasTag("project")
views:
  - type: table
    name: Projects
    order:
      - file.name
      - owner
      - status
      - due
    sort:
      - property: due
        direction: ASC
  - type: list
    name: Open
    filters:
      and:
        - status != "done"
```
````

PDF:

![A table view of the project notes, sorted by due date](../img/features/bases.png)

## Views

- `![[Books.base]]` and ` ```base ` blocks show the first view. `![[Books.base#Reading list]]` shows the view with that name.
- `table` and `cards` views become a table, `list` views a bullet list. Other view types (`kanban`, `map`, views of community plugins) become a table, and the export prints a warning.
- Columns come from the view's `order` (only the file name when there is none), with the `displayName` from `properties` as header.
- The file name links to the note when the note is part of the export. Otherwise it is plain text, see [links to pages outside the PDF](wiki-links.md#links-to-pages-outside-the-pdf).
- `sort` (several properties, `ASC` or `DESC`, empty values last), `limit`, `groupBy` (a label line and a table per group), `groupOrder` and the view's `summaries` (a last row such as `Sum: 25.5`) work.
- The global `filters` and the view's `filters` both apply. `and`, `or` and `not` can be nested. `this` is the note that shows the base.

## Expressions

| Area | Supported |
| ---- | --------- |
| Literals | numbers, `"text"` and `'text'`, `true`, `false`, `null`, lists `[1, 2]`, objects, regular expressions `/a.c/gi` |
| Operators | `+ - * / %`, `== != > < >= <=`, `&& \|\| !`, `a ? b : c`, parentheses, `x.y`, `x["y"]`, `list[0]` |
| Properties | `price`, `note.price`, `note["my price"]`, `formula.name`, `file.*`, `this.*`. A name with a `-`, such as `due-date`, is a property when the note has one, otherwise a subtraction. |
| File fields | `name`, `basename`, `path`, `folder`, `ext`, `size`, `ctime`, `mtime`, `properties`, `tags`, `links`, `embeds`, `backlinks` |
| File functions | `hasTag()` (nested tags count), `inFolder()`, `hasLink()`, `hasProperty()`, `asLink()` |
| Global functions | `if()`, `date()`, `duration()`, `now()`, `today()`, `number()`, `list()`, `link()`, `file()`, `min()`, `max()`, `escapeHTML()`, `image()` |
| Any value | `isTruthy()`, `isType()`, `isEmpty()`, `toString()` |
| Text | `length`, `contains()`, `containsAll()`, `containsAny()`, `startsWith()`, `endsWith()`, `lower()`, `title()`, `trim()`, `replace()` (text or regular expression, `$1`), `repeat()`, `reverse()`, `slice()`, `split()` |
| Numbers | `abs()`, `ceil()`, `floor()`, `round()`, `toFixed()` |
| Lists | `length`, `contains()`, `containsAll()`, `containsAny()`, `filter()`, `map()`, `reduce()` (with `value`, `index`, `acc`), `flat()`, `join()`, `reverse()`, `slice()`, `sort()`, `unique()`, `mean()`, `sum()`, `min()`, `max()` |
| Dates | `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `millisecond`, `date()`, `format()` (Moment.js tokens), `time()`, `relative()`, `date + "1M"`, `date - "2h"`, `date - date` (milliseconds) |
| Links | `asFile()`, `linksTo()`, comparing links with files and `this` |
| Objects | `keys()`, `values()` |
| Regular expressions | `matches()` |
| Summaries | `Average`, `Min`, `Max`, `Sum`, `Range`, `Median`, `Stddev`, `Earliest`, `Latest`, `Checked`, `Unchecked`, `Empty`, `Filled`, `Unique`, and custom summaries with `values` |

Anything else, such as `html()`, `icon()`, `random()` or a function that does not exist, is not dropped silently: the export prints a warning that names the base and the expression. A filter that cannot be evaluated is ignored, so the view shows more notes rather than fewer. A column that cannot be evaluated stays empty.

Property types come from the YAML: a date written as `2024-05-01` is a date. The types set in Obsidian (`.obsidian/types.json`) are not read. Dates are shown as `YYYY-MM-DD`, checkboxes as ☑ and ☐.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/

# Plugins

The third layer handles syntax and files from community Obsidian plugins and other tools. Each plugin support module lives in its own package under [`plugins/`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/tree/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins), is found through an entry point and runs inside the `plugins` step of the [core steps](../obsidian/index.md#order-of-the-steps).

## Built-in plugins

| Name | Obsidian plugin | What it does | Priority |
| ---- | --------------- | ------------ | -------- |
| `folder_notes` | [Folder Notes](https://github.com/LostPaul/obsidian-folder-notes) | `Folder/Folder.md` is the text of its folder. [More](folder-notes.md) | 5 |
| `dataview` | [Dataview](https://github.com/blacksmithgu/obsidian-dataview) | Runs DQL queries (`TABLE`, `LIST`, `TASK`, `CALENDAR`), inline queries, inline fields and DataviewJS. [More](dataview.md) | 10 |
| `excalidraw` | [Excalidraw](https://github.com/zsviczian/obsidian-excalidraw-plugin) | Turns drawing embeds into images. [More](excalidraw.md) | 15 |
| `meta_bind` | [Meta Bind](https://github.com/mProjectsCode/obsidian-meta-bind-plugin) | Fills `VIEW[...]` fields from the frontmatter, removes inputs and buttons. [More](meta-bind.md) | 20 |
| `block_link_plus` | [Block Link Plus](https://github.com/Jasper-1024/block-link-plus) | Resolves `![[Note#^id-id]]` range embeds. [More](block-link-plus.md) | 30 |
| `drawio` | [draw.io](https://www.drawio.com/) SVG exports | Turns HTML labels into SVG text. [More](drawio.md) | 40 |
| `citations` | [Citations](https://github.com/hans/obsidian-citation-plugin), Zotero integrations | Renders `[@key]` citations and a reference list with pandoc citeproc. [More](citations.md) | 50 |

```bash
ope list-plugins
```

shows the same list at runtime, including third-party plugins you installed.

## Turn a plugin off

```bash
ope export ./Vault --disable-plugin dataview --disable-plugin meta_bind
```

## Pass options

```bash
ope export ./Vault -O dataview.js-timeout=30
```

`-O key=value` reaches every plugin hook as `context.options`. Plugin options use the name of the plugin as prefix: `<plugin>.<key>`.

## Third-party plugins

Any Python package can register a plugin under the `obsidian_pdf_exporter.obsidian_plugins` entry point. After `pip install` (or `uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter --with <package>`) it is used without any change to ope. See [Write a plugin](write-a-plugin.md).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/folder-notes/

# Folder Notes

`ope export ROOT` walks the folder `ROOT`. Every subfolder becomes a section. The [Folder Notes](https://github.com/LostPaul/obsidian-folder-notes) plugin stores the note of a folder inside it, with the folder's name: `Chapter A/Chapter A.md`. The `folder_notes` plugin maps that note onto its folder while the page tree is built, so the note becomes the text of the folder's section. The root note `ROOT/ROOT.md` is the first text of the document.

Folder:

```text
folder-notes/
├── folder-notes.md       ← root note
├── Introduction/
│   └── Introduction.md   ← section 1
├── Part A/
│   ├── Part A.md         ← section 2
│   ├── Chapter 1/
│   │   └── Chapter 1.md  ← section 2.1
│   └── Chapter 2/
│       └── Chapter 2.md  ← section 2.2
└── Part B/
    └── Part B.md         ← section 3
```

PDF:

![Table of contents and numbered sections made from the folders](../img/features/folder-notes.png)

## Without the plugin

With `--disable-plugin folder_notes` the folders still become numbered sections, with the folder name as heading, but the sections have no text: `Folder/Folder.md` is not used.

## Sections, table of contents and numbering

- Sections are sorted by folder name. The folder name is the section heading.
- Headings are numbered and listed in the table of contents. `--no-toc` leaves out the table of contents.
- Headings inside a note nest under the section heading, so a note's `##` sits one level below its folder.
- `--include` and `--exclude` pick top-level subfolders by name.
- Folders without Markdown, such as attachment folders, are left out. `.git`, `.obsidian`, `.vscode` and every other dot folder are skipped.

## The root note

Three layouts are recognised:

1. `Handbook/Handbook.md` exists: it is the root note.
2. `Handbook/Handbook/Handbook.md` exists: the inner folder is the root, its siblings become sections.
3. Neither: the root has no text, the subfolders are the sections.

## The vault

Links, embeds and images are looked up in the whole vault, not only in the exported folder. The vault is the folder that holds `.obsidian`, or else the root of the git repository. When several files share a name, the one closest to the linking page wins: `Part A/img/logo.png` beats `images/logo.png` for every page inside `Part A/`.

## Other conventions

A third-party plugin can change the convention with the `find_folder_note` hook, for example to use `Folder/README.md` or the note with `folder-note: true` in its frontmatter. See [Write a plugin](write-a-plugin.md#hooks).

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/dataview/

# Dataview

The `dataview` plugin runs [Dataview](https://github.com/blacksmithgu/obsidian-dataview) at export time: ` ```dataview ` blocks, inline queries, inline fields and DataviewJS. The query language, the function library, the page model and the views are a port of the Dataview sources (version 0.5.68), so a query gives the same rows, columns and order as in Obsidian's reading view. The result is written into the page as Markdown, so links to notes that are part of the export become links inside the PDF (other notes are shown as plain text, see [links to pages outside the PDF](../obsidian/wiki-links.md#links-to-pages-outside-the-pdf)).

The examples query these notes:

````markdown
---
tags: [project]
status: active
owner: Ana
due: 2026-05-01
---
Notes about Website relaunch.
````

````markdown
---
mood: good
---
Worked on the launch. [hours:: 6]

- [x] Send the draft to Ana ✅ 2026-03-30
- [ ] Book the venue 📅 2026-04-03
    - [ ] Compare two offers
````

The query runs over the whole vault (the folder with `.obsidian`, or the git repository). Without a vault root the blocks stay as they are.

## TABLE

Markdown:

````markdown
```dataview
TABLE status, owner, due
FROM #project
SORT due ASC
```

```dataview
TABLE WITHOUT ID file.link AS "Project", due - date(today) AS "Time left"
FROM #project
WHERE status != "done"
SORT due ASC
```

```dataview
TABLE rows.file.link AS "Projects", length(rows) AS "Count"
FROM #project
GROUP BY status
```
````

PDF:

![Three tables: projects with status, owner and due date, the time left per project, and projects grouped by status](../img/features/dataview.png)

- `TABLE a, b`, with `AS "Name"` for a column header and `WITHOUT ID` to drop the first column.
- The first header shows the number of results, `File (3)`, as Dataview does. The `File` header is `tableIdColumnName` of the settings; after `GROUP BY` it is the name of the group.
- A list in a cell becomes a bullet list, an empty value shows `renderNullAs` (`-`), dates use `defaultDateFormat` and `defaultDateTimeFormat`, durations read like `3 months, 2 weeks`.
- Text values are Markdown, as in Obsidian: links, emphasis and lists in a property show as such.
- A query with no results shows Dataview's dashed box with "No results to show for table query." (`warnOnEmptyResult`).

## LIST

Markdown:

````markdown
```dataview
LIST
FROM "_notes/Projects"
WHERE status != "done"
```

```dataview
LIST owner + " (" + status + ")"
FROM #project
SORT file.name
```

```dataview
LIST rows.file.link
FROM #project
GROUP BY owner
```
````

PDF:

![Lists of projects, of projects with owner and status, and of projects grouped by owner](../img/features/dataview-list.png)

`LIST` shows the file link, `LIST expr` shows `link: value`, and `LIST WITHOUT ID expr` only the value. After `GROUP BY` the group is the first part.

## TASK

Markdown:

````markdown
```dataview
TASK
FROM "_notes/Journal"
WHERE !completed
GROUP BY file.link
```

```dataview
TASK
FROM "_notes/Journal"
WHERE due AND due < date(2026-04-05)
```
````

PDF:

![Open tasks of the journal grouped by note, and tasks due before a date](../img/features/dataview-task.png)

`TASK` lists the tasks of the selected notes, with their subtasks. A subtask that is also a result is shown once, under its parent. `GROUP BY` puts each group under a heading with its count. Any status other than a space shows a checked box, as in Dataview. The task fields are those of Dataview: `status`, `checked`, `completed`, `fullyCompleted`, `text`, `line`, `section`, `link`, `children`, `parent`, `tags`, `outlinks`, the page fields, and `due`, `completion`, `created`, `start` and `scheduled` from inline fields (`[due:: 2026-04-03]`) or from the emoji of the Tasks plugin (📅 ✅ ➕ 🛫 ⏳).

## CALENDAR

Markdown:

````markdown
```dataview
CALENDAR file.day
FROM "_notes/Journal"
```
````

PDF:

![Month grids of March and April 2026 with the journal notes on their days](../img/features/dataview-calendar.png)

Obsidian shows an interactive calendar of the current month. The PDF shows one month grid (Sunday first) for every month that has results, with the notes under their day.

## Inline queries and inline fields

Markdown:

````markdown
---
reviewer: Ben
Review Date: 2026-04-02
---
Reviewed by `= this.reviewer` on `= this.review-date`.
The website relaunch is owned by `= [[Website relaunch]].owner` and due in `= [[Website relaunch]].due - date(today)`.
Hours logged in the journal: `= [[2026-03-30]].hours + [[2026-04-02]].hours`.

Inline fields: [effort:: 3 days] and (approved:: true).
````

PDF:

![A paragraph with values from inline queries and two inline fields](../img/features/dataview-inline.png)

- `` `= expr` `` is replaced by the value of the expression, with `this` for the current note. The prefix is `inlineQueryPrefix` of the settings.
- `[key:: value]` shows the key and the value, `(key:: value)` only the value, rendered like reading view does when `prettyRenderInlineFields` is on. A field that fills a whole line, `key:: value`, stays as written.

## DataviewJS

Markdown:

````markdown
```dataviewjs
const projects = dv.pages("#project").sort(p => p.due, "asc");
dv.header(4, "Projects by owner");
for (const group of projects.groupBy(p => p.owner)) {
  dv.paragraph(`**${group.key}**: ${group.rows.file.name.join(", ")}`);
}
dv.table(["Project", "Due", "Done"],
  projects.map(p => [p.file.link, p.due, p.status === "done" ? "yes" : "no"]));
const open = dv.pages('"_notes/Journal"').file.tasks.where(t => !t.completed);
dv.paragraph(`Open tasks: ${open.length}`);
```

Open projects: `$= dv.pages("#project").where(p => p.status != "done").length`
````

PDF:

![A heading, owner lines, a table and two counts made by a DataviewJS script](../img/features/dataviewjs.png)

` ```dataviewjs ` blocks and `` `$= ...` `` inline queries run in an embedded V8 engine ([mini-racer](https://github.com/bpcreech/PyMiniRacer)), so no Node.js is needed. The `dv` object provides:

- data: `dv.pages(source)`, `dv.pagePaths()`, `dv.page()`, `dv.current()`, with Dataview's `DataArray` (`where`, `filter`, `map`, `flatMap`, `sort`, `groupBy`, `groupIn`, `distinct`, `limit`, `slice`, `first`, `last`, `array`, `length`, `values`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, and field access like `pages.file.name`),
- queries and expressions: `dv.query()`, `dv.tryQuery()`, `dv.queryMarkdown()`, `dv.execute()`, `dv.evaluate()`, `dv.tryEvaluate()`, `dv.func.*` (the DQL functions),
- output: `dv.table()`, `dv.list()`, `dv.taskList()`, `dv.header()`, `dv.paragraph()`, `dv.span()`, `dv.el()` (with `cls` and `attr`), `dv.container`, `dv.view()`, and `dv.markdownTable()`, `dv.markdownList()`, `dv.markdownTaskList()`,
- values: `dv.date()`, `dv.duration()`, `dv.fileLink()`, `dv.sectionLink()`, `dv.blockLink()`, `dv.parse()`, `dv.literal()`, `dv.compare()`, `dv.equal()`, `dv.array()`, `dv.luxon` (Luxon 3.4) and `dv.io.load()` and `dv.io.csv()` for files of the vault.

The script has no network, no `require`, no Obsidian `app` and no file writes; `dv.io` only reads files inside the vault. Every block has a time limit of 10 seconds (`-O dataview.js-timeout=30` changes it). An error is shown like in Obsidian (`Evaluation Error: ...`) and printed as a `Warning:`. A `dv.header()` is a heading that is not numbered and not in the table of contents.

## Queries

| Part | Supported |
| ---- | --------- |
| Query types | `TABLE` (`WITHOUT ID`, `AS`), `LIST` (`LIST expr`, `WITHOUT ID`), `TASK`, `CALENDAR` |
| Data commands | `WHERE`, `SORT` (several keys, `ASC`/`DESC`), `GROUP BY` (with `rows`), `FLATTEN`, `LIMIT`, in any order and repeated; `//` comments |
| Sources | `#tag` (nested tags count), `"folder"` or `"folder/note"`, `[[note]]` (notes that link to it), `outgoing([[note]])`, `csv("file.csv")`, combined with `and`, `or`, `-` or `!` and parentheses |
| Literals | numbers, `"text"`, `true`, `false`, `null`, `[lists]`, `{objects}`, `[[links]]`, `![[embeds]]`, `date(2026-04-01)`, `date(today)`, `date(now)`, `date(sow)` and the other shorthands, `dur(1 week 2 days)` |
| Operators | `+ - * / %`, `= != < > <= >=`, `and`, `or`, `!`, `a.b`, `a["b"]`, `list[0]`, `(x) => expr`, `row.field`, `this.field`, `[[note]].field` |
| Functions | all of Dataview's: `object`, `list`, `date`, `dur`, `number`, `string`, `link`, `embed`, `elink`, `typeof`, `round`, `trunc`, `floor`, `ceil`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `product`, `average`, `minby`, `maxby`, `contains`, `icontains`, `econtains`, `containsword`, `extract`, `sort`, `reverse`, `length`, `nonnull`, `firstvalue`, `all`, `any`, `none`, `join`, `filter`, `map`, `flat`, `slice`, `unique`, `reduce`, `regextest`, `regexmatch`, `regexreplace`, `replace`, `lower`, `upper`, `split`, `startswith`, `endswith`, `padleft`, `padright`, `substring`, `truncate`, `default`, `ldefault`, `display`, `choice`, `striptime`, `dateformat`, `durationformat`, `currencyformat`, `localtime`, `hash`, `meta` |

Values follow Dataview: functions work on each element of a list where Dataview does, comparisons of mixed types order by type, `null` sorts first, text sorts like `localeCompare`, dates and durations follow Luxon (a month is 30 days, `date - date` is normalised into years, months, weeks, days and time). A row whose expression fails is left out; when every row fails, the query shows Dataview's error text. A query that does not parse shows the parser error, and the export prints a `Warning:`.

## Pages

Every note has the `file` fields of Dataview: `name`, `folder`, `path`, `ext`, `link`, `size`, `ctime`, `cday`, `mtime`, `mday`, `tags` (with parent tags), `etags`, `inlinks`, `outlinks`, `aliases`, `lists`, `tasks`, `frontmatter`, `day` (from a `date` field or a date in the file name) and `starred` (from `.obsidian/bookmarks.json`).

Frontmatter properties are fields, with a normalised key next to the written one (`Due Date` is also `due-date`). Text that is a date, a duration or a link becomes one. Inline fields (`key:: value`, `[key:: value]`, `(key:: value)`) in paragraphs, headings and list items are fields too, with values parsed as numbers, dates, durations, links, booleans and lists.

`ctime` and `mtime` come from the file system, as for [Bases](../obsidian/bases.md). After a git checkout they are the checkout time, not the commit time.

The order of results without `SORT` is the order of the vault tree, folder by folder and case-insensitive (Obsidian uses the order it indexed the files in).

## Settings

The settings of the Dataview plugin are read from `.obsidian/plugins/dataview/data.json`: `renderNullAs`, `defaultDateFormat`, `defaultDateTimeFormat`, `tableIdColumnName`, `showResultCount`, `warnOnEmptyResult`, `maxRecursiveRenderDepth`, `inlineQueryPrefix`, `inlineJsQueryPrefix`, `enableInlineDataview`, `enableDataviewJs`, `enableInlineDataviewJs`, `prettyRenderInlineFields` and `dataviewJsKeyword`. Without the file the defaults of Dataview apply, except that DataviewJS is on. Each setting can be changed for one export:

```bash
ope export ./Vault -O dataview.renderNullAs=n/a -O dataview.enableDataviewJs=false
```

`-O dataview.now=2026-04-01T09:00` fixes `date(now)` and `date(today)`, so a PDF can be made again with the same content.

## Differences to Obsidian

- Interactive parts have no PDF form: tasks cannot be checked and the calendar is a static grid.
- Names of months and days are English (`en-US`), whatever the language of the system.
- `dv.func` functions get values, not JavaScript functions (`dv.func.map(list, x => ...)` does not work; use the `DataArray` methods). `dv.el()` elements support the common DOM methods but have no real browser behind them.
- An embed in a cell (`![[note]]`) is shown as a link; images are shown.
- `inlineQueriesInCodeblocks`: inline queries in fenced code blocks are not evaluated.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/excalidraw/

# Excalidraw

The `excalidraw` plugin turns embeds of [Excalidraw](https://github.com/zsviczian/obsidian-excalidraw-plugin) drawings into images.

Markdown:

````markdown
An Excalidraw drawing from the vault:

![[Drawing.excalidraw|420]]
````

PDF:

![An Excalidraw drawing with shapes, fills, an arrow, free drawing, text and an image](../img/features/excalidraw.png)

## Embeds

| Syntax | Finds |
| ------ | ----- |
| `![[Drawing.excalidraw]]`, `![[Drawing.excalidraw.md]]` | The drawing note `Drawing.excalidraw.md`. |
| `![[Drawing]]` | Any note with `excalidraw-plugin` in its frontmatter. |
| `![[Sketch.excalidraw]]` | A plain `.excalidraw` JSON file, as saved by excalidraw.com. |
| `![[Drawing.excalidraw\|400]]` | A width, as for images. |

## Auto-export files first

When the plugin's "Auto-export SVG" or "Auto-export PNG" setting wrote `Drawing.excalidraw.svg` (or `.light.svg`, `.png`, `.light.png`) next to the drawing, that file is used as it is. It looks exactly like the drawing in Obsidian. `-O excalidraw.auto_export=off` turns this off.

## Drawn from the scene

Otherwise ope reads the scene from the `## Drawing` section of the note (a ` ```json ` block, or ` ```compressed-json ` in LZ-String base64) and draws it as SVG. Excalidraw's hand-drawn look comes from rough.js in the browser. ope draws the same shapes with clean strokes, so the export needs neither Node.js nor a browser.

| Drawn | Not drawn (with a warning) |
| ----- | -------------------------- |
| Rectangles (also rounded), diamonds, ellipses | Embedded web pages, shown as an outlined box with their link |
| Solid fills; hachure, cross-hatch and zigzag fills as straight hatching | LaTeX equations |
| Lines, curves, elbow arrows and all arrowheads | Embedded notes, PDFs and drawings inside a drawing |
| Free drawing, as a line of even width | Image cropping (the whole image is drawn) |
| Text, also inside shapes and on arrows | Element links and `#^group=`, `#^area=`, `#^frame=` parts of an embed (the whole drawing is shown) |
| Images from the vault or a data URL, mirrored images | |
| Stroke colour, width, dashed and dotted strokes, opacity, rotation | |

Frames are not drawn, as in an Excalidraw export. Text uses the Excalidraw fonts when they are installed and falls back to a sans-serif or monospace font. The frontmatter keys `excalidraw-export-transparent` and `excalidraw-export-padding` are honoured. Dark drawings are drawn with their light colours.

For an exact copy of the hand-drawn look, turn on auto-export in the Excalidraw plugin.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/meta-bind/

# Meta Bind

The `meta_bind` plugin fills [Meta Bind](https://github.com/mProjectsCode/obsidian-meta-bind-plugin) `VIEW` fields with the values of the page's frontmatter. `INPUT` and `BUTTON` fields have no PDF form and are removed.

Markdown:

````markdown
---
product: Example App
version: 2.4.0
released: 2026-04-15
platforms: |
  - Linux
  - macOS
---
Release notes for `VIEW[{product}][text]` version `VIEW[{version}][text]`.

Released on `VIEW[{released}][date(D MMMM YYYY)]` (`VIEW[{released}][date(DD.MM.YYYY)]`).

| Field     | Value                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Product   | `VIEW[{product} + " " + {version}][text]` |
| Platforms | `VIEW[{platforms}][text]`                 |

Input fields such as `INPUT[text:version]` are removed.
````

PDF:

![View fields filled with the frontmatter values](../img/features/meta-bind.png)

- `{key}` is the value of a frontmatter field. `+` joins values and quoted text.
- `[date(D MMMM YYYY)]` and `[datetime(DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm)]` format an ISO date or date and time with moment.js tokens: `D`, `DD`, `M`, `MM`, `MMM`, `MMMM`, `YY`, `YYYY`, `H`, `HH`, `mm` and `ss`. Month names are English. Other text in the format is kept. A value that is not a date is shown as written.
- A multi-line value shown inside text, such as in a table cell, stays in its cell: list items become an HTML list, other lines are joined with line breaks. A field alone on its line keeps the lines as they are.
- Fields inside code blocks are left as written.
- In an embedded note, the fields use the embedded note's frontmatter.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/block-link-plus/

# Block Link Plus

[Block Link Plus](https://github.com/Jasper-1024/block-link-plus) extends block references to ranges: `^id` marks the first block, `^id-id` the last one. `![[Note#^id-id]]` embeds everything from the first to the last block. The source note:

````markdown
# Procedure

Before the range.

1. Check out the repository. ^steps
2. Run the export.
3. Review the PDF. ^steps-steps

After the range.
````

Markdown:

````markdown
The steps from the procedure:

![[Procedure#^steps-steps]]
````

PDF:

![Only the steps of the range are embedded](../img/features/block-link-plus.png)

The end marker can also sit on its own line below a block, for example after a list or table. When the first line of a range is empty, Block Link Plus writes a `%% %% ^id` placeholder, which also works. Without this plugin, `^id-id` is looked up as a plain block ID.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/drawio/

# draw.io

draw.io stores labels as HTML in `<foreignObject>`, which WeasyPrint does not draw. Next to each label it writes a short fallback text and a "Text is not SVG - cannot display" note. The `drawio` plugin replaces each label with SVG text, one `<tspan>` per line, and removes the note.

Markdown:

````markdown
A draw.io diagram exported as SVG with HTML labels:

![[flow.drawio.svg]]
````

PDF:

![A draw.io diagram with readable labels](../img/features/drawio.png)

This is a best effort:

- Mixed formatting inside one label (a bold word, a second colour) is flattened to the main style of the label.
- Wrapped labels are wrapped again with an estimated character width, so line breaks can differ a little from draw.io.
- For full fidelity, export from draw.io with "Convert labels to SVG" turned on, or as PNG.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/citations/

# Citations

The `citations` plugin renders [pandoc citations](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#citation-syntax) with `pandoc --citeproc`, as the [Citations](https://github.com/hans/obsidian-citation-plugin) plugin and the Zotero integration plugins write them. The bibliography of this example is `examples/_attachments/references.bib`.

Markdown:

````markdown
---
bibliography: ../_attachments/references.bib
---
Typesetting is covered in depth by [@knuth1984, p. 12].
Several sources at once: [see @knuth1984; @lamport1995].
@lamport1995 shows how to structure a proof.

## References
````

PDF:

![Citations in the text and the reference list](../img/features/citations.png)

| Written | Rendered (default Chicago author-date style) |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `[@doe2020]` | (Doe 2020) |
| `[@doe2020, p. 12]` | (Doe 2020, 12) |
| `[see @doe2020; @roe2021]` | (see Doe 2020; Roe 2021) |
| `[-@doe2020]` | (2020) |
| `@doe2020 shows` | Doe (2020) shows |

## Bibliography

The bibliography is the first one found of:

1. `-O citations.bibliography=refs.bib` (several files separated by `,`). Relative paths start at the current folder or the exported folder.
2. The export path of the Citations plugin: `citationExportPath` in `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-citation-plugin/data.json`, relative to the vault.
3. `bibliography:` in the frontmatter of the exported notes (a path or a list), relative to the note.

BibLaTeX and BibTeX (`.bib`, `.bibtex`), CSL JSON (`.json`) and CSL YAML (`.yaml`) work.

## Options

| Option | Effect |
| ------ | ------ |
| `-O citations.bibliography=PATH` | Bibliography files, separated by `,`. |
| `-O citations.csl=PATH` | A [CSL style](https://www.zotero.org/styles). `csl:` in the frontmatter does the same. |
| `-O citations.title=TEXT` | Heading of the reference list when ope adds one. |
| `-O citations=off` | Leave citations as written. |

## Where the reference list goes

The list goes into a `::: {#refs}` block when the document has one, otherwise below the last heading named `References`, `Bibliography`, `Works cited`, `Literature` or `Sources`. Without either, a `References` heading and the list are added at the end. Citations link to their entry.

`@word` outside brackets becomes a citation only when `word` is a key of the bibliography, so `@mentions` and e-mail addresses stay text. A link to a literature note such as `[[@doe2020]]` becomes the in-text citation `@doe2020` when the note is not part of the export.

Without a bibliography, citations stay as written and the export prints one warning. A citation whose key is not in the bibliography also prints a warning, and pandoc shows it as `(doe2020?)`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/plugins/write-a-plugin/

# Write a plugin

A plugin support module is a subclass of [`ObsidianPlugin`](https://github.com/Spenhouet/obsidian-pdf-exporter/blob/main/obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/base.py) that overrides the hooks it needs. It can live in this repository or in a package of its own. Support for core Obsidian syntax is a step, not a plugin, see [Contributing](../contributing.md).

## Example: strip Tasks metadata

The [Tasks](https://github.com/obsidian-tasks-group/obsidian-tasks) plugin adds emoji metadata such as `📅 2026-05-10` to task lines. This plugin removes it:

```python title="my_ope_plugins/tasks.py"
from __future__ import annotations

import re

from obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.base import ObsidianPlugin
from obsidian_pdf_exporter.plugins.base import PluginContext

_METADATA = re.compile(r"\s+[⏫🔼🔽📅⏳🛫✅❌🔁][^\n]*")

class TasksPlugin(ObsidianPlugin):
    """Remove the emoji metadata of the Tasks plugin."""

    name = "tasks"
    description = "Remove Tasks plugin metadata from task lines"
    priority = 60  # after the built-in plugins (5 to 50)

    def process_markdown(self, content: str, context: PluginContext) -> str:
        return _METADATA.sub("", content)
```

Register it under the entry point group in the package's `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project.entry-points."obsidian_pdf_exporter.obsidian_plugins"]
tasks = "my_ope_plugins.tasks:TasksPlugin"
```

Install it next to ope and check that it is found:

```bash
uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter --with ./my-ope-plugins
ope list-plugins
```

## Hooks

All hooks have no-op defaults.

| Hook | Runs | Used by |
| ---- | ---- | ------- |
| `find_folder_note(folder)` | While the page tree is built. Returns the note of a folder or `None`. The first plugin with a result wins. | `folder_notes` |
| `process_markdown(content, context)` | On each page and on embedded notes, after the frontmatter is parsed and before embeds, callouts and wiki links. | `dataview`, `meta_bind`, `excalidraw` |
| `process_document(markdown, context)` | On the assembled Markdown of the whole document, after `process_markdown` ran on every page. | `citations` |
| `reader_extensions(context)`, `pandoc_args(context)` | When the pandoc call is built, after `process_document`. Return extra reader extensions and arguments, such as `--citeproc`. | `citations` |
| `extract_block(body, block_id)` | For `![[Note#^id]]`. Returns the selected text or `None`, before core looks for `^id`. | `block_link_plus` |
| `process_svg(svg, context)` | On each SVG image while it is inlined. | `drawio` |
| `process_html(html, context)` | On the HTML of the whole document, after the core HTML steps and before the template. | `meta_bind` |

`PluginContext` (markdown hooks) has `vault_root`, `page_folder`, `frontmatter`, `options` and `vault_index`. `vault_root` is `None` when the export runs outside a vault, so a plugin that needs vault-wide data should do nothing then.

`DocumentContext` (SVG and HTML hooks) has `build_dir`, `options`, `root`, `export` (title, version, date), `template`, `plugins`, `redline` and `log`.

## Priority

`priority` is an integer, lower runs earlier. The built-ins use 5 (`folder_notes`), 10 (`dataview`), 15 (`excalidraw`), 20 (`meta_bind`), 30 (`block_link_plus`), 40 (`drawio`) and 50 (`citations`). Pick a value after the plugins whose output you need: a plugin that reads tables made by Dataview runs after 10.

## Guarantees

- The frontmatter is parsed and removed before `process_markdown` runs.
- Plugins run before embeds, callouts, wiki links and image captions, so their output passes the rest of the pipeline like written Markdown.
- Plugins also run on embedded notes, with the context of the embedded note.
- Keep code as written. Wrap a rewrite in `outside_code` from `obsidian_pdf_exporter.core.code`, as Obsidian does not process code.

## In this repository

A plugin for a broadly used Obsidian plugin can go into `obsidian_pdf_exporter/plugins/<name>/` with an `__init__.py` that exports the class and a thin `plugin.py`. Put larger parsing code in a module next to it, as Dataview does with `engine.py`. Add the entry point to the project's `pyproject.toml`, unit tests in `tests/unit/`, a page in these docs and an example in `examples/`.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/redline/

# Redline

`ope redline` builds a tracked-changes PDF of a folder between two git commits, or between two folders or notes on disk. Inserted text is blue and underlined, removed text is vermilion and struck through, moved text is purple, and a bar in the margin marks every change. The rest of the document is exactly as it is in the newer commit, so a reader sees every change in context, in the same layout as the released PDF.

```bash
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0 --to-commit v1.1.0
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0 -O redline.style=side-by-side   # old | new in two columns
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0 -O redline.collapse=on          # only the changes
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0 --blame                         # who changed what, and why
ope redline ./Policy --from-path ./old/Policy                             # two folders, no git
```

![Before, after and redline of a short policy, next to each other](../img/redline/redline-three-up.png)

## Who it is for

A redline answers "what changed since the version I approved?" without a diff tool and without reading Markdown. Typical uses:

- Document control: every new release of a procedure, policy or manual goes out with a redline against the previous release.
- Reviews and approvals: the reviewer of a pull request reads the redline PDF instead of the raw diff.
- Audits: the change history of a controlled document can be shown for any two versions, at any time, from the git history.
- Change requests: the PDF of a proposed change is attached to the request, so the people who decide see the exact wording.

## How it works

1. Both commits are taken from git with `git archive`. Uncommitted changes in the working tree are not part of either version. With `--from-path`, both versions are read from disk instead.
2. Each version of the folder is assembled into one Markdown document with the same steps and plugins as `ope export`. Embeds are expanded, Dataview queries run and Meta Bind values are filled in, so the two documents are compared as they appear in the PDF.
3. The two documents are split into blocks at blank lines (paragraphs, list blocks, tables, headings, code blocks) and the blocks are compared.
4. Blocks that are alike are paired. A paired block is compared word by word (lists item by item, tables cell by cell, code line by line) and gets inline `<ins>` and `<del>` marks. A block that only exists in one version is shown as a whole inserted or removed block, and a block that was removed in one place and inserted in another is shown as moved.
5. The result goes through the rest of the export (callouts, links, numbering, table of contents). Then the change summary is added and the document is laid out in the chosen [style](styles.md), with the [`redline` template](styling.md).

## What the reader sees

![Redline of the example policy](../img/redline/overview.png)

- A change summary after the title: the two versions, the number of changes of each kind, the changed sections with their page numbers and the commits in between.
- Inserted words: blue with a double underline. Removed words: vermilion and struck through. A replaced passage shows the old words, then the new ones.
- Inserted and removed blocks (paragraphs, list items, table rows, callouts, figures, code lines) are marked the same way as a whole; a removed figure is faded and labelled.
- Moved text: purple, with a link from each end to the other.
- A black bar in the left margin next to every group of changed blocks.
- Changed headings show their word changes, also in the table of contents, which counts the changes per section, marks new sections and lists removed headings struck through. A changed heading level gets a small label.
- The [side-by-side style](styles.md#side-by-side) shows the old and the new document in two aligned columns instead.

[What changes look like](changes.md) shows every kind of change in both styles.
## In this section

| Page | Content |
| ---- | ------- |
| [Usage](usage.md) | The command and every flag, default names, one document or a folder, and CI workflows. |
| [Comparing versions](compare.md) | Tags, branches, commits and `HEAD~n`, releases, pull requests, the history of one note, and two folders or notes without git. |
| [Styles and options](styles.md) | Blackline and side by side, collapsing unchanged content and the blame strip, with every combination. |
| [What changes look like](changes.md) | Words, paragraphs, headings, lists, tables, callouts, images, embeds, properties and Dataview, each in both styles. |
| [Blame](blame.md) | The author, date and commit message of each block next to the page, for exports and redlines. |
| [Styling the redline](styling.md) | The `redline` template, the classes and variables a redline uses, and how to restyle them. |
| [Limitations and tips](limitations.md) | What a redline does not show, and how to get a clean one. |

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/redline/usage/

# Usage

```text
ope redline ROOT --from-commit REF [--to-commit REF] [OPTIONS]
ope redline ROOT --from-path PATH [OPTIONS]
```

`ROOT` is the folder to compare, the same folder `ope export` takes, or a single note. With `--from-commit`, the command must run inside the git repository that holds `ROOT`, and both commits must be in its history. With `--from-path`, `ROOT` is the newer version on disk and `PATH` the older one, and no git is needed (see [Without git](compare.md#without-git)).

```bash
cd MyVault                      # anywhere inside the repository
ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit v1.0.0
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- | ------- |
| `--from-commit REF` | | The older version, the baseline, as a git commit. |
| `--to-commit REF` | `HEAD` | The newer version, as a git commit. |
| `--from-path PATH` | | The older version as a folder or note on disk; `ROOT` on disk is the newer one. Not together with `--from-commit`, `--to-commit` or `--blame`. |
| `-o PATH`, `--output PATH` | `./.export/<title>_redline.pdf` | Where the PDF goes. `.export/` is made in the current folder. |
| `-t TEXT`, `--title TEXT` | the folder name, or the note name | Title on the first page and in the header. |
| `--subtitle TEXT` | `Changes from <from> to <to>` | Replaces the subtitle. The version label in the footer keeps the hashes (or the names of the two folders or notes). |
| `-T NAME\|PATH`, `--template NAME\|PATH` | `redline` | Another template, see [Styling the redline](styling.md). |
| `-O redline.style=STYLE` | `blackline` | `blackline` or `side-by-side`, see [Styles and options](styles.md). |
| `-O redline.collapse=on` | off | Show only the changes and the headings of their sections. |
| `-O KEY=VALUE`, `--option KEY=VALUE` | | Other options for steps, plugins and the template, as for `export`. |
| `--blame` | off | A strip next to every page with the author, date and commit message of each changed block, see [Blame](blame.md). Needs `--from-commit`. |
| `--disable-plugin NAME` | | Skip a plugin in both versions. |
| `--toc/--no-toc` | `--toc` | Table of contents at the start. |
| `--debug` | off | Keep the build folder `_build_<name>/` next to the PDF, with `redline_assembled.md` (the diffed Markdown) and `redline_final.html`. |

`export` flags that have no meaning for a redline, such as `--version`, `--date`, `--include` and `--exclude`, are not available. The date in the footer is the day of the export. The full list is in the [CLI reference](../reference/cli.md#redline).

## Which versions

`--from-commit` and `--to-commit` take tags, branches, commit hashes and relative refs such as `HEAD~3`. Both sides are read from git, so uncommitted changes are not included. When `ROOT` does not exist in one of the two commits, that side counts as empty: a folder that is new since `--from-commit` comes out as one big insertion. [Comparing versions](compare.md) has the details: releases, pull requests and the history of one note.

`--from-path` compares two folders or two notes on disk instead, without git:

```bash
ope redline ./Handbook --from-path ./archive/Handbook
```

## Output name and title block

Without `-o`, the PDF is `./.export/<title>_redline.pdf`, for example `.export/Handbook_redline.pdf`. With `--title "Team handbook"` it is `.export/Team handbook_redline.pdf`. With `.` as `ROOT` the title is the name of the current folder.

The title block names the two versions as they were given, and the footer has the short hashes and the date:

```text
Handbook
Changes from v1.0.0 to HEAD
```

`--subtitle "Changes since release 1.0"` replaces the second line. The change summary below the title lists both commits with their hashes, dates and authors, and the commits in between.

## One document or a whole folder

`ROOT` decides what is compared. A folder with subfolders gives one redline of the whole document, with all sections and one table of contents. A section folder gives a redline of that section alone.

```bash
ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit v1.0.0                  # the whole handbook
ope redline ./Handbook/Security --from-commit v1.0.0         # one section
```

A redline for each top-level folder:

```bash
for folder in Policies/*/; do
  ope redline "$folder" --from-commit v1.0.0 -o "out/$(basename "$folder") redline.pdf"
done
```

## In CI

The checkout needs the history of both commits, so set `fetch-depth: 0`. Install ope and its native libraries the same way as for [exports in CI](../getting-started/installation.md#in-ci).

### A redline for every pull request

This workflow builds the redline of a pull request against the point where it left the base branch, uploads it as an artifact and links it in a comment on the pull request:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/redline-pr.yml"
name: Redline

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "Handbook/**"

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  redline:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # both commits must be in the history
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - run: uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter
      - run: ope setup --yes

      - name: Build the redline
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          base=$(git merge-base "origin/$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_SHA")
          ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit "$base" --to-commit "$HEAD_SHA" -o redline.pdf

      - name: Upload the PDF
        id: upload
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: redline
          path: redline.pdf

      - name: Link the PDF in the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          URL: ${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-url }}
        run: |
          gh pr comment "$PR" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --body "Redline PDF of this pull request: $URL"
```

The token of a pull request from a fork cannot write comments. For those, keep the upload step and drop the comment step.

### A redline attached to every release

This workflow runs when a release is published. It compares the tag of the release with the tag before it and attaches the PDF to the release:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/redline-release.yml"
name: Redline release

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

permissions:
  contents: write # to upload the PDF to the release

jobs:
  redline:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # all tags and their history
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - run: uv tool install obsidian-pdf-exporter
      - run: ope setup --yes

      - name: Build the redline against the previous release
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          previous=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 "$TAG^")
          ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit "$previous" --to-commit "$TAG" \
            --subtitle "Changes from $previous to $TAG" -o "Handbook $TAG redline.pdf"

      - name: Attach the PDF to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: gh release upload "$TAG" "Handbook $TAG redline.pdf" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
```

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/redline/compare/

# Comparing versions

A redline compares two versions of a folder or a note. They come from one of two places:

- Git: `--from-commit` names the older commit and `--to-commit` the newer one (default `HEAD`). The command runs inside the repository, and both commits must be in its history.
- Disk: `--from-path` names an older copy of the folder or note, and `ROOT` is the newer one, both read as they are on disk. No git is needed. See [Without git](#without-git).

The two ways cannot be mixed: `--from-path` is refused together with `--from-commit` or `--to-commit`.

## Git refs

Both flags take anything git resolves to a commit:

| Ref | Example | Compares |
| --- | ------- | -------- |
| Tag | `--from-commit v1.0.0 --to-commit v1.1.0` | Two releases |
| Branch | `--from-commit main` | The tip of `main` with `HEAD` |
| Remote branch | `--from-commit origin/main` | The fetched tip of `main` with `HEAD` |
| Commit hash, full or short | `--from-commit 3f2c9a1` | One commit with `HEAD` |
| Relative ref | `--from-commit HEAD~3`, `--from-commit v1.1.0^` | Three commits back, or the commit before a tag |
| Date | `--from-commit 'main@{2026-01-01}'` | `main` as it was on a date (from the reflog, so only in a clone that has seen it) |

Both sides are read from git, never from the working tree. Uncommitted changes are not part of either version, so commit them first.

A range such as `v1.0.0..v1.1.0` is not accepted: name the two ends with the two flags. An unknown ref stops the command with exit code 1 and the error from git.

## Releases

A release against the previous release:

```bash
ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit v1.0.0 --to-commit v1.1.0
```

The latest tag against the tag before it:

```bash
new=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)
old=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 "$new^")
ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit "$old" --to-commit "$new" --subtitle "Changes from $old to $new"
```

## A branch or pull request against main

A reviewer wants the changes of the branch alone. Compare against the merge base, the commit where the branch left `main`:

```bash
ope redline ./Handbook --from-commit "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)"
```

`--from-commit main` also shows, reversed, every change made on `main` since the branch was created.

## The history of one note or folder

`git log` with a path lists the commits that changed it. Pick two of them:

```bash
git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -- Handbook/Security
ope redline ./Handbook/Security --from-commit 3f2c9a1 --to-commit 8b41d07
```

`ROOT` can also be a single note. Then only that note is compared, as a document of one page:

```bash
ope redline ./Handbook/Security/Security.md --from-commit 3f2c9a1
```

A redline of the parent folder still shows the changes of the whole document, with every section.

The last commit that changed a folder against the one before it:

```bash
last=$(git log -1 --format=%h -- Handbook/Security)
ope redline ./Handbook/Security --from-commit "$last^" --to-commit "$last"
```

## In CI

The checkout must hold the history of both commits: `fetch-depth: 0` in `actions/checkout`. The [Usage](usage.md#in-ci) page has complete GitHub Actions workflows that attach a redline to a pull request (against the merge base) and to a release (against the previous tag).

## Without git

`--from-path` compares two folders, or two notes, as they are on disk. `ROOT` is the newer version and `--from-path` the older one:

```bash
ope redline ./Handbook --from-path ./archive/handbook-1.0/Handbook          # folder against folder
ope redline ./Handbook/Security.md --from-path ./old/Security.md            # note against note
```

Both must be folders, or both must be notes. Neither side has to be in git, and uncommitted changes are included because the files are read from disk. This also compares the working tree with an older copy, or two exports of a vault from different places.

Each side is read in its own vault: links, embeds and images are looked up from the closest folder above it that holds `.obsidian` (or `.git`). Without such a folder, the folder of the side itself is the vault, so notes and images outside of it are not found. Copy the whole vault, or at least its `.obsidian` folder and the attachments, when the folder embeds files from elsewhere. A copy of an old version made with `git archive` keeps the vault together:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/handbook-1.0
git archive v1.0.0 | tar -x -C /tmp/handbook-1.0
ope redline ./Handbook --from-path /tmp/handbook-1.0/Handbook
```

The change summary names both paths as they were given, each with the date of the newest file in it (`(folder, modified 2026-03-30)`), and lists no commits. The subtitle is `Changes from <old path> to <new path>` unless `--subtitle` replaces it. `--blame` needs the git history of both versions and is refused with `--from-path`.

Two PDFs cannot be compared: ope reads the Markdown, not the PDF.

---

Source: https://spenhouet.com/obsidian-pdf-exporter/redline/styles/

# Styles and options

A redline has two looks and two options that work with both:

| Option | Values | What it does |
| ------ | ------ | ------------ |
| `-O redline.style=` | `blackline` (default), `side-by-side` | Changes marked in the text of the new version, or the old and the new document in two aligned columns. |
| `-O redline.collapse=` | `off` (default), `on` | Show only the changes and the headings of their sections; each run of unchanged text becomes one line. |
| `--blame` | off | A strip next to every page with the author, date and commit message of the last change of each block. See [Blame](blame.md). |

```bash
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0                                  # blackline
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0 -O redline.style=side-by-side    # two columns
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0 -O redline.collapse=on           # only the changes
ope redline ./Policy --from-commit v1.0.0 --blame                          # who changed what
```

Every redline starts with a change summary after the title: the two versions with their commits, dates and authors, the number of replaced, inserted, deleted and moved passages and of other changes (formatting, link targets, heading levels, tasks), the changed sections with their page numbers, and the commits between the two versions. The table of contents shows the number of changes next to each changed section, marks new sections with "new" and lists removed headings struck through.

## Blackline

The default. The document is the new version, with every change marked where it happened:

- Inserted text is blue with a double underline, removed text vermilion and struck through. A replaced passage shows the old words followed by the new ones.
- Moved text is purple: struck through where it was, underlined where it is now. A label at each end names the section of the other end and links to it.
- A black bar in the left margin marks every group of changed blocks.
- Formatting changes, link targets, task states and heading levels get a dotted underline or a small label.

The colours are chosen so that inserted and removed text stay apart for readers with red-green colour blindness, and every change also has a form that survives greyscale printing (underline, strike-through, bar).

![First page of a blackline redline with the change summary](../img/redline/page-blackline.png)

## Side by side

The old and the new document in two columns on landscape pages, in the page size of the template turned on its side (A4 landscape by default). Images are scaled down to the width of their column. Every block of the document sits on its own row, so the old and the new version of a paragraph, a list item or a table always start at the same height. A block that exists in only one version faces a hatched gap ("not in the old version", "deleted", "moved"). Every list item has a row of its own, so a long list stays aligned and can break between pages.

A thin bar between the columns marks the rows that changed; a moved block has a dashed purple bar. Word changes are marked in both columns: removed words in the old column, inserted words in the new one.

![First page of a side-by-side redline](../img/redline/page-side-by-side.png)

## Collapse unchanged content

With `-O redline.collapse=on` the redline shows only what changed. The heading of every section that contains a change stays, so the reader knows where a change is. Each run of unchanged blocks becomes one quiet line, for example "⋯ 2 paragraphs unchanged ⋯" or "⋯ unchanged: 4 Contact (1 paragraph) ⋯". Inside a changed list or table, a run of unchanged items or rows is collapsed the same way. Links from the table of contents, the summary and the text to collapsed headings and blocks still work: they point to the collapsed line. In the side-by-side style, a chapter without changes becomes one such line in the table of the chapter before it. A link to a heading that is not in the PDF at all, such as `[[#Typo]]`, stays as plain text, and the command prints a warning.

In the side-by-side style every row shown is a change, so the bar between the columns is left out.

## Every combination

The example below is a short policy with changed list items, a table with a new row, a changed paragraph and two sections that did not change. The version before was written by one author, the change by another, so the blame strip has two names.

Before:

````markdown
## Scope

This policy applies to all laptops of the team. It covers how devices are handed out, used and returned.

## Rules

- Lock the screen when you leave the desk.
- Install updates once a week.
- Use the password manager for all accounts.
- Store work files on the shared drive.
- Report a lost device within one day.

## Devices

| Device | Owner      | Review |
| ------ | ---------- | ------ |
| Laptop | IT team    | yearly |
| Phone  | Each user  | yearly |

## Contact

Questions go to the service desk. The service desk answers within one working day.

## Exceptions

Test devices are exempt from the update rule.
````

After:

````markdown
## Scope

This policy applies to all laptops of the team. It covers how devices are handed out, used and returned.

## Rules

- Lock the screen when you leave the desk.
- Install updates once a month.
- Use the password manager for all accounts.
- Store work files on the shared drive.
- Report a lost or stolen device within one hour.
- Ask the service desk when in doubt.

## Devices

| Device | Owner      | Review    |
| ------ | ---------- | --------- |
| Laptop | IT team    | quarterly |
| Phone  | Each user  | yearly    |
| Tablet | IT team    | yearly    |

## Contact

Questions go to the service desk. The service desk answers within one working day.

## Exceptions

Test devices in the lab are exempt from the update rule. They must not hold customer data.
````
